🚬 THE LINCOLN PENNY THAT CAME IN PACKS OF CIGARETTES

One day in 1955, a press at the Philadelphia Mint began striking Lincoln cents from a flawed die. The date and the words LIBERTY and IN GOD WE TRUST came out boldly doubled.

By the time an inspector caught it late in the afternoon, numismatist Q. David Bowers wrote, more than 40,000 had been made. Coins still in the box were destroyed, but about 24,000 had already been mixed with normal cents, and the Mint let them go.

Many turned up in Massachusetts and upstate New York. Cigarettes cost 23 cents in vending machines that took only quarters, so vendors tucked two pennies inside the cellophane as change. Some smokers found the doubled cents right there.

A Seat for Putin, No Deal for Ukraine

Donald Trump said he would bring up the war in Ukraine at Thursday’s summit in Shenzhen. Vladimir Putin came away from the opening with something more immediate. He sat beside Trump and Xi Jinping at the first summit of the three countries’ leaders.

Trump met Putin separately before the summit and called him “my friend.” Their previous meeting, in Alaska in August 2025, ended with the prospect of a later agreement on Ukraine. No such deal materialized. Russia has since escalated its attacks, and Western intelligence assessments cited by The New York Times expect Moscow to keep fighting at least through the winter.

Trump has business of his own with Xi. He wants China to extend a trade truce that expires in January and to keep rare earth materials and magnets flowing to the United States. Xi gets to host both presidents in Shenzhen, a Chinese technology hub, and put China at the center of a meeting Washington once would have expected to convene itself.

All three leaders spoke about the responsibilities of nuclear powers. Officials cautioned against expecting a major breakthrough. Putin did not need one. He got the seat and the photograph before offering anything on Ukraine.
